pos.personaBrief: De Zerbi's sides had the highest Serie A possession share in 2020/21 and over 70% in several Brighton games, and he says the most important thing is to have the ball. Baiting is about giving the opponent a reason to press, not about giving up the ball.

pro.personaBrief: The goalkeeper acts as a third centre-back, 94% of goal kicks are short, and Dunk puts his foot on the ball to wait for the press. The break forward is fast, but only after the press has been drawn out.

est.personaBrief: Sassuolo used triangle rotations with a 2+3 build-up and Brighton collapsed into a compact 4-2 or 4-1 core. The 2-3-5 shape stays defined, but players rotate and drop to combine.

lar.personaBrief: After drawing the press, Brighton use maximum width, with full-backs hugging the touchlines and wingers isolating defenders, and 40% of attacks come down the left. The bait is central, but the finish is wide.

blo.personaBrief: Sassuolo pressed very aggressively with a man-oriented first wave and counter-pressed everywhere, and Brighton defended high with full-backs jumping to press. He calls pressing a gamble, but the profile never sits deep and wants to counter-press after losing the ball.

mar.personaBrief: The pressing is described as man-to-man (Premier League, Left Back Football) with strikers marking centre-backs, though Sassuolo also used a zonal 4-4-2. Corner and star-marking habits are not documented.

pla.personaBrief: He says he has a clear idea in his head of how his team should play and imposes it on arrival, as at Brighton. He adapts only in small ways, such as a 3-5-2 against tougher Sassuolo opponents.

res.personaBrief: He plays with courage, wants the ball, and gets praise for entertaining football (Guardiola: best build-up in the world). His teams keep the same approach when ahead and away from home, and are criticised for being leaky.

sis.personaBrief: The method rests on strict structural duties for everyone, and defenders are the key to the build-up. He also says the level of the players matters most, and forwards like Mitoma are free to keep trying.

jog.personaBrief: He wants technical midfielders and defenders who can receive under pressure close to goal, such as Gilmour, Mac Allister and Caicedo. He also wants athletic full-backs and midfielders for the aggressive pressing.

bas.personaBrief: Many youngsters developed under him at Sassuolo (Left Back Football), and he complained about Brighton's recruitment. The sources give no sign that he favours academy players over signings, or veterans over youth.

lid.personaBrief: He decides the line-up his own way and thanks Bloom for the freedom. He gives players such as Trossard and Solly clear responsibilities, and the evidence is thin on discipline and dressing-room atmosphere.
